newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Panalpina strategy changes to target new markets.
newsitem.headline: Panalpina strategy changes to target new markets.

text.p: Swiss freight-forwarding concern Panalpina Welttransport AG said it plans to make changes in its business strategy to expand in selected areas.
In a statement, Panalpina said it also named Bruno Sidler, head of Panalpina's Air Sea Broker unit, to succeed Gerhard Fischer as its chief executive officer, effective May 1998.
"Panalpina plans over the next few years to become the world's premier supplier of transport services to the oil and energy, electronics and telecommunications and automotive industries," it said.
"It also intends to substantially expand the logistics services it provides for deparment store groups," it said.
It said the key to its strategy will be "integrated forwarding," which in the airfreight field has meant it has taken a postion between integrators and traditional forwarders.

It said the concept, which is used by Air Sea Broker, would be extended to sea freight. The integrated forwarding concept would be backed by expansion in areas of electronic data management, procurement and transport insurance.
It is also introducing a new group structure in various countries which streamlines the existing structure.
These include combining U.S. and Canadian units to form a new North American unit, headed by Rolf Altorfer, currently chief executive of Panalpina U.S.A.
Panalpina is one of Switzerland's three largest freight forwarders.
